reader.explanation: The parameterized reduction to Max-Cut constructs a clique-width expression. Adding as many isolated vertices as the Max-Cut graph has vertices converts the instance to Maximum Bisection. Complementation then sends a lower threshold b on the resulting 2n-vertex graph to the upper threshold n²−b. The complement expression is constructible from the original expression with at most twice as many labels. An algorithm for intrinsic clique-width can ignore the expression. Its parameter factor can be replaced by a computable nondecreasing majorant because intrinsic width is at most the expression width.
